comments.author: SuccessIsHardWork
comments.body: What game engine did you use? I’m vibecoding a game currently and I couldn’t get it to look good on any other than the web.

replies.author: Alarmed_Profit1426
replies.body:
Same boat, no engine. Just Next.js + HTML5 canvas with a custom ECS for 2D, plus three.js for the 3D mode. Honestly I think web is the right call for vibecoding right now: way more training data for canvas / three.js / web stack than for Unity or Godot, so Claude actually knows what it's doing instead of confidently hallucinating engine APIs that don't exist.

Iteration loop helps too, instant reload, browser devtools, deploy and share with a link. If you want a "real" desktop build later, Tauri wraps the whole web app into a native binary without rewriting anything. Best of both worlds!
